File: src/world.rs:422
Summary: No World::phase_feeding-level test verifies that a non-predator/prey pair (e.g. same element, or a ring-adjacent-but-wrong-direction pair) never triggers a feeding event — the asymmetric-ring guarantee is only exercised at the element.rs unit-test level, never through an actual World tick.

Severity claimed: low

content.text: Confirmed: no test anywhere (world.rs's own `mod tests`, or tests/ecology.rs) constructs a non-predation pair (same element, or wrong-direction ring pair) in reach and asserts `stats.feedings` stays 0. All feeding-related tests construct an actual Fire-eats-Wood predator/prey pair. The ring-asymmetry guarantee (`nothing_beats_itself_and_the_two_edges_never_coincide`) is indeed only exercised at the `element.rs` unit level, verifying `Element::eats()` in isolation — never through an actual `World::step`/`phase_feeding` call that would catch a bug in how `phase_feeding` itself derives `(pred, prey)` from `a.eats() == b` / `b.eats() == a`.

input.reasoning:
Verified by reading src/world.rs (phase_feeding, lines 422-516) and its full test module (mod tests, especially lines 807-846), plus tests/ecology.rs in its entirety. Every existing feeding-related test constructs a genuine predator/prey pair (Fire eats Wood) and asserts feedings == 1 or > 0; none constructs a non-predation pair (same element, or a ring pair where neither eats() the other) in reach and asserts stats.feedings stays 0. grep confirms 'feedings' only appears in the two positive-case assertions in world.rs and one aggregate '>0' assertion in tests/ecology.rs — no negative-case check exists at the World level.

The ring-asymmetry guarantee cited by the finding (nothing_beats_itself_and_the_two_edges_never_coincide) lives only in src/element.rs's own unit tests, which test Element::eats()/beats() directly and would not catch a bug introduced in phase_feeding's own derivation logic (the `if a.eats() == b {...} else if b.eats() == a {...} else {continue}` block at lines 444-450) — e.g. an accidental `||` instead of correct branching, a copy-paste swap of a/b, or an off-by-one if that logic were ever rewritten to do its own ring index math instead of delegating to eats(). This is a real, reachable gap in test coverage: a regression localized to phase_feeding's pair-derivation would slip through the entire existing test suite (both src/world.rs unit tests and tests/ecology.rs integration tests), since none of them ever place two elements that should NOT feed on each other within forage_radius and assert feedings stays 0. The severity (low) is reasonable given it's a coverage gap rather than a live bug, and the fix is cheap (one small test). I stand behind this as genuine and reachable.
